areas.name: Left overhead console
areas.text: The ceiling panel above the pilot's side. It holds the weapons panels, the anti-ice panel, the R-863 channel selector and the pilot's intercom box.

panels.name: Pilot's upper weapons control panel
panels.text: The upper weapons panel above the pilot. It shows which weapons are loaded and ready, and holds the main weapon switch, the emergency jettison and the sight brightness knob.
panels.context: The pilot sets it before an attack. The master arm switch for the weapons is on the circuit breaker console; with it off, nothing can be fired or dropped.

controls.name: PKV sight brightness knob
controls.text: This knob sets how bright the aiming mark in the PKV sight is. The PKV is a glass sight in front of the pilot with a ring and marks.
controls.context: The manual says the default is 50 percent. The pilot turns it up in bright daylight.

controls.name: Upper weapons panel lamp check button
controls.text: Pressing this button lights all lamps of the pilot's upper weapons panel, to show that no bulb is burned out.
controls.context: The pilot presses it during the preflight check.

controls.name: RKT-GUN MASTER switch (RS/GUV selector)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The weapon fire circuits are powered.

controls.text: This is the main switch for the rockets, the cannon pods and the gun containers. With it off, they cannot fire.
controls.context: The manual says to set it on during the attack run. It powers the fire circuits and the loaded and ready lamps.

controls.name: FCU ARM button (PUS arming)
controls.text: Pressing this button gets the rocket fire control units ready, so that the first rocket flies from tube number 1. It is held until the armed lamps appear.
controls.context: It works only when the RKT-GUN MASTER switch is on, the circuit breakers are on and the rocket weapon is chosen.

controls.name: Minelaying system master switch

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The mine system master is on; it has no effect in DCS.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The mine system master is off.

controls.text: This is the main switch of the mine laying system, which would drop mines from the helicopter.
controls.context: The manual says the mine system is not implemented in the simulation.

controls.name: Jettison ARMED switch and cover

positions.name: ON
positions.text: Jettisoned bombs are armed to explode on impact.

controls.text: This guarded switch decides whether dropped bombs are armed. When it is on, jettisoned bombs will explode on impact.
controls.context: The ARMED lamp lights when it is on. A cover protects the switch.

controls.name: Emergency jettison switch and cover
controls.text: This guarded button drops everything the helicopter carries on its outside racks. The pilot lifts the cover first.
controls.context: The manual says it frees all weapon stations, quickly lowering the weight in an emergency such as a forced landing.

controls.name: Weapons status lamps and ammunition counters
controls.text: This part of the upper panel shows lamps for which stations carry weapons and which rocket units are ready. Counters show the rounds left in the guns.
controls.context: The manual says some counters show a fraction of the real number, for example the cannon counter shows half of the rounds.

panels.name: Pilot's lower weapons control panel
panels.text: The lower weapons panel chooses what the FIRE button on the cyclic shoots and how: rockets, cannon pods or gun containers, and how many or how long.
panels.context: The pilot sets it with the copilot's payload panel before an attack, because the gun containers need the copilot's payload setting.

controls.name: Rockets quantity switch (8 / 16 / 4)
controls.text: This switch sets how many rockets leave each rocket pod while the fire button is held down.
controls.context: The manual gives an example: with two pods loaded and the switch on 4, up to 8 rockets are fired.

controls.name: Rocket station selector (1-2-5-6 / AUTO / 3-4)

positions.text: Rockets are fired from stations 1, 2, 5 and 6.
Rockets are fired from stations 3 and 4.

controls.text: This switch chooses which weapon racks fire their rockets.
controls.context: The manual says in AUTO mode the outer racks fire first and the inner racks 3 and 4 follow when they are empty.

controls.name: Weapon selector (UPK / PKT / RS)

positions.name: PKT
positions.text: The nose machine gun; not implemented in DCS.

controls.text: This switch chooses what the FIRE button shoots: the cannon pods, the nose machine gun or the rockets.
controls.context: The manual says the nose machine gun (PKT) is not implemented. The gun containers have their own selector.

controls.name: GUV cutoff switch

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The gun containers fire in bursts set by the burst knob.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The gun containers fire as long as the trigger is held.

controls.text: This switch decides if the gun containers fire as long as the trigger is held, or in short bursts.
controls.context: In burst mode the length is set with the burst knob next to it.

controls.name: GUV burst length knob
controls.text: This knob sets how long one burst of the gun containers lasts, in seconds. Short is 0.25 seconds, medium 0.6.
controls.context: A longer burst means more rounds in one burst.

controls.name: GUV fire selector

positions.text: Grenades or the 12.7 mm machine gun on stations 2 and 5.
The 7.62 mm machine guns on stations 2 and 5.

controls.text: This switch chooses which gun containers fire: grenade launchers or machine guns on the different stations.
controls.context: The manual says it is used with the GUV payload selector. The positions are 800, 800 plus 624 and 622.

controls.name: GUV payload selector and cover

positions.text: A mixed load of machine guns and grenade launchers.

controls.text: This switch tells the system what kind of gun containers are fitted. A cover protects it.
controls.context: The manual says to set 800 when only grenade launchers are loaded and the mixed position when stations 1 and 6 have grenade launchers and 2 and 5 machine guns.

controls.name: YakB-12.7 gun charging switches (left, right)
controls.text: These two switches reload the 12.7 mm machine guns in the gun pods if they jam. Each has three positions for the guns I, II and III.
controls.context: The manual says the switch must be put to position I before firing.

controls.name: Gun camera switch
controls.text: This switch turns on the gun camera, which records a picture each time the pilot fires.
controls.context: The manual says the gun camera records whenever the weapon fire switch is pressed.

panels.name: Anti-ice (defrost) system control panel
panels.text: The panel that switches on the heating against ice for the front windows, the engine air intakes and the rotor blades.
panels.context: The pilot uses it in cold, wet weather. The automatic mode starts the heating when the ice detector senses ice.

controls.name: Anti-ice GENERAL MANUAL-AUTO switch

positions.name: AUTO
positions.text: The ice detector starts the anti-ice heating.

positions.name: MANUAL
positions.text: The pilot switches the heating on by hand.

controls.text: This switch picks the main mode of the anti-ice system. In AUTO the ice detector switches the heating on. In MANUAL the pilot switches parts on himself.
controls.context: The manual says that in automatic mode all switches on the panel are put down.

controls.name: Anti-ice OFF button
controls.text: Pressing this button turns the whole anti-ice system off.
controls.context: The manual says to put all switches down and press this button to switch the system off.

controls.name: Left engine heater switch (PSS left)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The left engine intake heating is on.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The left engine intake heating is off.

controls.text: This switch heats the air intake and the dust separator of the left engine so ice cannot form.
controls.context: The manual says this heating is always switched on and off by hand, and should be on before flight in cold weather.

controls.name: Right engine heater switch (PSS right)

positions.name: AUTO
positions.text: The ice detector can start the heating.

positions.name: MANUAL
positions.text: The heating is switched on by hand.

controls.text: This switch heats the air intake and the dust separator of the right engine. It can work by hand or by the ice detector.
controls.context: The manual says the right engine heating can start by hand or automatically.

controls.name: Glass heater switch

positions.name: AUTO
positions.text: The ice detector can start the window heating.

positions.name: MANUAL
positions.text: The window heating is switched on by hand.

controls.text: This switch heats the two front windows to keep them free of ice and fog.
controls.context: The manual says the windows are kept at about 30 degrees.

controls.name: Ice detector heater switch

positions.name: AUTO
positions.text: The detector heater runs by itself.

positions.name: MANUAL
positions.text: The detector heater is switched on by hand.

controls.text: This switch heats the ice detector itself, the small sensor that senses ice.
controls.context: The game names it the Ice Detector Heater Switch with positions MANUAL and AUTO.

controls.name: Ice detector heater test button
controls.text: Pressing this button tests the heater of the ice detector. A lamp shows if the heater works.
controls.context: It belongs to the check of the anti-ice system.

controls.name: Ammeter load selector switch
controls.text: This rotary switch picks which part of the anti-ice heating the ammeter dial measures: windows, engine intakes or the rotor blade sections.
controls.context: The manual says the ammeter readings of the main rotor and tail rotor must be divided by 3 and 6 to get the true current.

controls.name: Anti-ice lamps (normal, icing, ON, rotor sections)
controls.text: These lamps show if the anti-ice system works, whether ice is detected, whether the heating is on, and which rotor blade section is being heated now.
controls.context: The red icing lamp flashes with the flasher system when the ice detector senses ice.

controls.name: AF1-150 ammeter
controls.text: This dial shows the electric current of the selected anti-ice heater.
controls.context: The pilot checks that the current stays inside the range given in the manual.

panels.name: R-863 modulation and channel selector
panels.text: Two controls of the main radio R-863 in the ceiling: how the voice is carried, and which of the 20 stored channels is used.
panels.context: The pilot sets the channel and the type of modulation before talking to another station. The type must match the other station.

controls.name: R-863 modulation switch (FM / AM)
controls.text: This switch picks the radio way the voice is carried: FM or AM. Both stations must use the same one to hear each other.
controls.context: The manual shows FM as the up position and AM as the down position.

controls.name: R-863 channel selector
controls.text: This knob picks one of the stored radio channels. Each channel is a frequency prepared on the ground.
controls.context: The manual says there are 20 channels, and the channel table is set in the DCS mission editor. The channels are used with the unit switch on MEMORY.

panels.name: SPU-7 intercom control box (pilot)
panels.text: The SPU-7 is the intercom, the telephone line between the crew members. It also decides which radio the pilot talks on and how loud the sounds are.
panels.context: The pilot sets the radio source before talking. The cyclic trigger then speaks on the intercom or the chosen radio.

controls.name: SPU-7 RADIO / ICS switch (pilot)

positions.name: RADIO
positions.text: The second trigger click transmits on the radio.

positions.name: ICS
positions.text: The trigger always talks on the intercom.

controls.text: This switch decides what the trigger on the cyclic does: talks on the intercom or on the chosen radio.
controls.context: The manual says with RADIO set, the first click of the trigger uses the intercom and the second click uses the radio.

controls.name: SPU-7 circular call button (pilot)
controls.text: In the real helicopter this button calls all crew stations at doubled volume, for emergency messages. The game marks it N/F, not functional.
controls.context: The manual lists it as the ALL CALL button.

controls.name: SPU-7 network 1/2 switch (pilot)
controls.text: This switch would pick between two intercom networks. The manual says it is not used.
controls.context: The pilot's switch of this kind has no function in DCS; the copilot has a twin.

controls.name: SPU-7 radio source selector (pilot)
controls.text: This rotary knob picks which radio the pilot listens to and talks on: the R-863, the Yadro-1A, the R-828 or the radio direction finders ARK-9 and ARK-UD.
controls.context: The manual says the right source must be picked before the radios work through the headset.

controls.name: SPU-7 common (master) volume knob (pilot)
controls.text: This knob sets the loudness of the intercom for the pilot.
controls.context: The manual says the master and monitor knobs swap roles when the RADIO/ICS switch changes.

controls.name: SPU-7 listening (monitor) volume knob (pilot)
controls.text: This knob sets the loudness of the radio the pilot listens to.
controls.context: The manual says the two volume knobs swap roles when the RADIO/ICS switch changes.

areas.name: Center overhead console
areas.text: The ceiling panel in the middle. It holds the fire protection, the APU, the fuel pumps, the engine start and the hydraulic switches, and the engine fuel levers.

panels.name: Fire protection system panel
panels.text: This panel shows where a fire is and lets the pilot fire the extinguisher bottles. The helicopter has two bottles: the first bottle fires by itself, the second one is for another fire.
panels.context: If a fire lamp lights up, the first bottle usually goes off automatically. If it does not, the pilot presses the button of the burning place. Test switches check the detectors.

controls.name: First order (main) discharge buttons (left engine, right engine, KO-50, APU/gearbox)
controls.text: These four buttons empty the first extinguisher bottle into one place: the left engine, the right engine, the KO-50 heater or the APU and main gearbox compartment.
controls.context: The first bottle normally fires by itself. The pilot presses the button of the burning place if it does not.

controls.name: Second order (alternate) discharge buttons (left engine, right engine, KO-50, APU/gearbox)
controls.text: These four buttons empty the second extinguisher bottle into one place. It is the reserve for a second fire or if the first did not work.
controls.context: The manual says the second bottle is fired by hand only.

controls.name: Fire signal OFF button (alarm silence)
controls.text: Pressing this button silences the fire alarm lamp after the fire is out. The manual calls it the alarm silence button.
controls.context: The pilot presses it if the fire lamp does not go out by itself within about 10 seconds.

controls.name: Fire detector test switch (EXTINGUISH / TEST)

positions.name: EXTINGUISH
positions.text: The fire system is ready for fighting a fire.

positions.name: TEST
positions.text: The fire sensors can be tested with the rotary switch.

controls.text: This switch changes the fire system between normal readiness and a test of the fire sensors. In the test position a lamp lights.
controls.context: The manual says the system must be in the EXTINGUISH position to work in flight. Test the sensors on the ground before start.

controls.name: Squib test switch (I / II)

positions.name: I
positions.text: Checks the charges of the first bottle.

positions.name: II
positions.text: Checks the charges of the second bottle.

controls.text: This switch tests the small charges that open the extinguisher bottles. Position I checks the first bottle and II the second.
controls.context: The manual says that no yellow lamp should light if the charges are good.

controls.name: Check fire circuits switch (OFF / CONTROL / 1-6)
controls.text: This rotary switch checks the fire sensor groups one channel at a time. Each position should make the matching fire lamps light.
controls.context: The manual says to turn it back to OFF afterwards and to keep it there so the first bottle does not fire by accident.

controls.name: Fire protection annunciators
controls.text: These lamps show a fire in the left engine, right engine, KO-50 heater or the transmission and APU compartment, and that a bottle has fired.
controls.context: The red fire lamps flash. A voice also speaks the place of the fire.

panels.name: APU start control panel (AI-9V)
panels.text: The APU is a small extra engine at the back. It makes the compressed air that spins the main engines for starting, and can also make electricity. This panel starts and stops it.
panels.context: The APU is started first. The manual says to let it run at least one minute before starting the main engines, then shut it off when both engines run.

controls.name: APU start mode switch (START / COLD CRANKING / FALSE START)

positions.name: START
positions.text: A normal start of the APU.

positions.name: COLD CRANKING
positions.text: Turns the APU over without a start.

positions.name: FALSE START
positions.text: Runs the start cycle without ignition, for example to clear a failed start.

controls.text: This switch picks what the next push of the start button does: really start, only spin the APU without fuel, or spin it after a failed start.
controls.context: The manual calls the positions START, CRANK and FALSE START. The normal start uses START.

controls.name: APU START button
controls.text: Pressing this button for two to three seconds starts the automatic start of the APU.
controls.context: The AUTO IGNITION lamp lights, then the APU runs up to idle in under 20 seconds.

controls.name: APU OFF button
controls.text: Pressing this button for two to three seconds stops the APU. It also aborts a start.
controls.context: The pilot shuts the APU down after both main engines are running.

controls.name: APU EGT and APU air pressure gauges
controls.text: These dials show the exhaust gas temperature of the APU and the air pressure it makes for starting the main engines.
controls.context: The manual says the temperature must be read times 100 and stay below 880 degrees during start. The air pressure should be 1.3 to 2.0 at idle.

panels.name: Fuel system control panel
panels.text: The panel for the fuel pumps and valves. Fuel is stored in two side tanks and a small feed tank behind the main gear. Pumps move it, and valves can shut each line off.
panels.context: Before start the pilot switches the pumps on and checks that their lamps light. In flight the pilot checks the pump lamps and the fuel left.

controls.name: Left shutoff valve switch (guarded)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The valve is open and the left engine gets fuel.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The valve is closed and the left engine gets no fuel.

controls.text: This guarded switch opens and closes the left emergency fuel shutoff valve. Closed, no fuel flows to the left engine.
controls.context: A lamp below the switch shows the closed valve. The valves are closed in a fire; the pilot lifts the cover first.

controls.name: Right shutoff valve switch (guarded)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The valve is open and the right engine gets fuel.

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The valve is closed and the right engine gets no fuel.

controls.text: This guarded switch opens and closes the right emergency fuel shutoff valve. Closed, no fuel flows to the right engine.
controls.context: A lamp below the switch shows the closed valve. The pilot lifts the cover first.

controls.name: Crossfeed switch (guarded)

positions.name: ON
positions.text: The connection between the two side tanks is open.

controls.text: This guarded switch opens or closes the connection between the left and the right side tank. Fuel can then flow from one to the other.
controls.context: The manual says the normal position is open. It is shut when one tank is damaged, to save the fuel in the other. A yellow lamp shows when it is shut.

controls.name: Bypass switch (guarded)
controls.text: This guarded switch opens a bypass valve, a backup path for fuel from the side tanks to the feed tank. It is only for the case that the float valve fails.
controls.context: The manual says the normal position is closed. With it open, the pilot must watch the fuel in the feed tank.

controls.name: Feed tank pump switch (FLOW)

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The feed tank pump is off.

controls.text: This switch turns on the pump of the feed tank, the small tank that feeds the engines. A green lamp shows it works.
controls.context: The manual says the pilot switches it on before starting the APU. The engines can still get fuel by gravity if it fails.

controls.name: Left tank pump switch

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The left tank pump is off.

controls.text: This switch turns on the pump in the left side tank. It moves fuel to the feed tank.
controls.context: The manual says to turn off a failed pump; the other pump can fill the feed tank alone.

controls.name: Right tank pump switch

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The right tank pump is off.

controls.text: This switch turns on the pump in the right side tank. It moves fuel to the feed tank.
controls.context: The manual says the pilot checks the pump lamps in flight.

controls.name: Refueling control switch (REFUEL / OFF / CHECK)

positions.name: REFUEL
positions.text: Refuelling mode of the full-tank lamps.

positions.name: CHECK
positions.text: Lamp check of the full-tank lamps.

controls.text: This switch sets the lamps that show a full tank during refuelling on the ground.
controls.context: The manual says these lamps are near the filler necks and are not implemented in the simulator.

panels.name: Engine start control panel
panels.text: The panel for starting the two main engines. A start computer runs the steps by itself after the pilot picks the mode and the engine and presses START.
panels.context: The APU must run first. After the start button, the pilot opens the fuel shutoff lever of the engine when the engine speed rises.

controls.name: Engine start mode switch (START / OFF / COLD CRANKING)

positions.name: COLD CRANKING
positions.text: Turns the engine over without starting it.

controls.text: This switch picks what the start does: a real start, or only turning the engine over without fuel and fire.
controls.context: The manual calls the second mode CRANK or false start. The normal start uses START.

controls.name: Engine selector switch (LEFT / OFF / RIGHT)
controls.text: This switch chooses which of the two engines the start button starts.
controls.context: The manual says to start the engine on the downwind side first.

controls.name: Engine START button
controls.text: Pressing this button for two to three seconds begins the automatic start of the chosen engine.
controls.context: The AUTO IGNITION and STARTER lamps light during the start. If the engine is not at 55 percent speed after 55 seconds, the start is aborted.

controls.name: Abort engine start button
controls.text: Pressing this button stops the engine start at any time.
controls.context: The pilot uses it when something looks wrong during start.

controls.name: Engine ignition check switch (LEFT / OFF / RIGHT)

positions.name: LEFT
positions.text: Checks the left engine ignition; springs back.

positions.name: RIGHT
positions.text: Checks the right engine ignition; springs back.

controls.text: This spring switch checks the ignition of the left or the right engine. The game names it 'Engine Ignition Check Switch'.
controls.context: The manual does not describe this switch.

panels.name: Hydraulic system control panel
panels.text: Hydraulics is oil under high pressure that helps the pilot move the heavy rotor controls. The helicopter has a main system and a backup system, with a switch for each.
panels.context: Both switches are normally on. If the main system fails, the backup takes over by itself and a red lamp lights.

controls.name: Main hydraulic system switch

positions.name: OFF
positions.text: The main hydraulic system is off and the backup takes over.

controls.text: This switch turns the main hydraulic system on and off. A green lamp shows that it is working.
controls.context: The manual says that if it is switched off the backup takes over and its red lamp lights.

controls.name: Backup (auxiliary) hydraulic switch (guarded)
controls.text: This guarded switch turns the backup hydraulic system on and off. A cover protects it.
controls.context: The backup is normally left on, so that it can take over by itself when the main system fails.

controls.name: Backup hydraulic OFF button
controls.text: Pressing this button switches from the backup system back to the main system. It is held for one to one and a half seconds.
controls.context: The manual says that during engine start the backup may switch on first; this button then returns to the main system.

controls.name: Main and backup hydraulic pressure gauges
controls.text: These dials show the pressure of the main and the backup hydraulic system. The reading must be multiplied by 10.
controls.context: The manual says the normal reading is 45 to 68 kg/cm2 for the working system.

panels.name: Engine fuel shutoff levers
panels.text: Two levers over the pilot that open and close the fuel to each engine. Forward is open and aft is closed (STOP).
panels.context: The pilot opens a lever when the engine starts spinning and closes it to shut the engine down.

controls.name: Left engine stop lever

positions.name: FORWARD
positions.text: Fuel flows to the left engine.

positions.name: AFT
positions.text: Fuel is cut off and the engine stops.

controls.text: This lever opens or closes the fuel to the left engine. Pulling it back stops the engine.
controls.context: The manual says it is moved forward when the engine speed starts to rise during start.

controls.name: Right engine stop lever

positions.name: FORWARD
positions.text: Fuel flows to the right engine.

positions.name: AFT
positions.text: Fuel is cut off and the engine stops.

controls.text: This lever opens or closes the fuel to the right engine. Pulling it back stops the engine.
controls.context: The pilot uses it for the start and when shutting down.

areas.name: Right overhead console
areas.text: The ceiling panel above the copilot's side. It holds the radio direction finders ARK-9 and ARK-UD, the gyro compass panel and the cabin heater.

panels.name: ARK-9 automatic direction finder (ADF) control panel
panels.text: The ARK-9 is a radio compass for beacons that send on medium waves (150 to 1300 kHz). It points a thin needle on the heading dial toward the beacon, and lets the pilot hear the beacon's name in Morse code.
panels.context: The pilot sets the beacon's frequency, then turns the mode to COMP. The panel has a main and a reserve channel, so the pilot can prepare the next beacon while using the first.

controls.name: ARK-9 mode selector (OFF / COMP / ANT / LOOP)

positions.name: COMP
positions.text: The needle points to the beacon; main working mode.

positions.name: ANT
positions.text: Only listens to the beacon; no direction.

positions.name: LOOP
positions.text: Listens through the loop antenna to find the direction by ear.

controls.text: This rotary switch turns the ADF on and picks its way of working: compass, antenna or loop.
controls.context: COMP is the main mode and shows the direction to the beacon. ANT is for listening and tuning, and LOOP is a backup that finds the direction by listening to the signal fade.

controls.name: ARK-9 VOICE / CW switch (TLF / TLG)
controls.text: This switch picks what kind of signal the ADF listens for: a voice or music signal, or an unvoiced continuous tone.
controls.context: The manual says VOICE listens to a broadcasting station and the beacon name, and CW is for a continuous wave signal.

controls.name: ARK-9 loop control switch (LEFT / OFF / RIGHT)

positions.name: LEFT
positions.text: Turns the loop to the left; springs back.

positions.name: RIGHT
positions.text: Turns the loop to the right; springs back.

controls.text: This spring switch turns the search loop antenna by hand to the left or right.
controls.context: The manual says the pilot can use it to check that the bearing needle follows when the antenna is turned.

controls.name: ARK-9 volume (GAIN) knob
controls.text: Turning this knob makes the beacon sound in the headset louder or quieter.
controls.context: The manual says to set it to maximum when tuning.

controls.name: ARK-9 channel selector (MAIN / BACKUP)
controls.text: This switch picks which of the two stored frequencies the ADF uses: the main channel or the backup (reserve) channel.
controls.context: The pilot can set the next beacon on the unused channel and then switch over.

controls.name: ARK-9 main channel frequency dials (100 kHz, 10 kHz)
controls.text: These two dials set the frequency of the main channel: the first the hundreds of kilohertz, the second the tens.
controls.context: The pilot dials the beacon frequency here and listens to its call letters.

controls.name: ARK-9 backup channel frequency dials (100 kHz, 10 kHz)
controls.text: These two dials set the frequency of the backup (reserve) channel in the same way.
controls.context: They let the pilot prepare a second beacon.

controls.name: ARK-9 fine tune knobs (main, backup)
controls.text: These two knobs fine-tune the frequency of the main and of the backup channel a little up or down.
controls.context: The manual says they move the frequency by -10 to +20 kHz.

panels.name: ARK-UD VHF homing set control panel
panels.text: The ARK-UD is a radio finder for VHF and UHF stations, made to find downed crews with a small emergency radio. It points the bearing needle on the heading dial toward the signal.
panels.context: The pilot picks the band and channel and uses the narrow or wide mode. A beacon must be placed in the mission for the ARK-UD to work in the game.

controls.name: ARK-UD mode selector (OFF / NARROW / WIDE / PULSE / RC)

positions.name: PULSE
positions.text: Receives a pulse signal on 243 MHz.

positions.name: RC
positions.text: Not used according to the manual.

controls.text: This rotary switch turns the ARK-UD on and picks how it listens. Narrow band is for a steady signal, wide band when close to the station.
controls.context: The manual says the pilot starts with narrow band and goes to wide when the WIDE lamp lights near the beacon. RC is not used.

controls.name: ARK-UD channel selector (1-6)
controls.text: This rotary switch picks one of six stored VHF frequencies.
controls.context: The manual lists them as 114.166, 114.333, 114.583, 121.5, 123.1 and 124.1 MHz. In the UHF band the channel does not matter.

controls.name: ARK-UD band switch (MW / DW, VHF / UHF)

positions.name: MW
positions.text: VHF band; use the channel selector.

controls.text: This switch picks the VHF or the UHF band of the ARK-UD.
controls.context: The game labels the positions MW and DW (metre wave and decimetre wave); the manual calls the switch FQ BAND with VHF up and UHF down.

controls.name: ARK-UD sensitivity switch (MORE / LESS)
controls.text: This switch sets how sensitive the homing receiver is.
controls.context: The manual calls it the sensitivity HIGH-LOW switch.

controls.name: ARK-UD volume knob
controls.text: Turning this knob makes the sound of the homing set louder or quieter.
controls.context: The pilot hears the beacon tone in the headset when the SPU-7 source is set to the ARK-UD.

controls.name: ARK-UD test (control) button
controls.text: Pressing this button runs the self-test of the ARK-UD. The needle on the heading dial should point to about 180 degrees.
controls.context: It is part of the check before flight.

controls.name: ARK-UD left and right antenna buttons
controls.text: These two buttons turn the loop antenna by hand to the left or to the right.
controls.context: The pilot can use them to test or help the direction finding.

panels.name: PU-26 gyro compass (GMK-1A) control panel
panels.text: The GMK-1A is the gyro compass, the helicopter's main heading system. This panel sets its mode, the home latitude and the course.
panels.context: The pilot sets the hemisphere and latitude, tests the system, and aligns it to the right magnetic direction before take-off. The power switch is on the right triangular panel.

controls.name: GMC hemisphere switch (NORTH / SOUTH)
controls.text: This switch tells the compass if the helicopter is in the northern or the southern half of the world.
controls.context: The manual says to set it to the current hemisphere before use.

controls.name: GMC latitude knob
controls.text: This knob sets the latitude, how far north or south the helicopter is. The compass uses it to cancel the effect of the Earth turning.
controls.context: The pilot sets it to the current latitude during the preparation.

controls.name: GMC mode switch (MK / GPK / AK)

positions.name: DG
positions.text: Directional gyro mode (GPK), the main mode.

controls.text: This switch picks how the compass finds north: by the magnetic compass (MK), by the gyroscope (GPK) or by the astrocompass (AK).
controls.context: The manual says GPK is the main mode. Switching from GPK to MK aligns the gyro quickly with the magnetic heading.

controls.name: GMC control (test) switch (0 / CONTROL / 300)
controls.text: This spring switch tests the compass by turning the indication to 0 or 300 degrees. The reading must come back within 10 degrees.
controls.context: It also lights the BANK CORR lamp during the test.

controls.name: GMC course set switch (CCW / OFF / CW)

positions.name: LEFT
positions.text: Turns the card counter-clockwise; springs back.

positions.name: RIGHT
positions.text: Turns the card clockwise; springs back.

controls.text: This spring switch turns the compass card of the heading dial left or right to line it up with the right direction.
controls.context: In the manual this is the course setting selector, used to set the heading in GPK mode.

panels.name: KO-50 cabin heater control panel
panels.text: The KO-50 is a kerosene burner that warms the cockpit and the cargo cabin. This small panel starts it, picks the mode and the temperature, and shows its status.
panels.context: The pilot uses it in cold weather: set automatic mode, set the temperature, press START. The heater needs its circuit breaker on the right breaker panel.

controls.name: KO-50 mode switch (MANUAL / OFF / AUTO)

positions.name: MANUAL
positions.text: The heat output is picked by hand.

positions.name: AUTO
positions.text: The heater holds the temperature set by the knob.

controls.text: This switch picks how the heater works: automatic at a set temperature, or by hand, or off.
controls.context: The manual says the neutral position switches the heater off after use.

controls.name: KO-50 heat output switch (FILLING / FULL / MEDIUM)
controls.text: This switch picks the heat output in manual mode: full or medium. The third position is for servicing.
controls.context: The manual says the priming position is for maintenance and is not modelled.

controls.name: KO-50 heater START button
controls.text: Pressing this button starts the heater. Lamps show the preheating, the igniter and that the heater runs.
controls.context: The manual says that after the preheater lamp goes out the ignition lamp should go out in under 40 seconds, which shows stable burning.

controls.name: KO-50 fan switch (ventilation)
controls.text: This switch runs the heater's fan alone, to blow fresh air through the cabin without heat.
controls.context: The manual says it is for ventilation in summer and for cooling the heater before it is switched off.

controls.name: KO-50 target temperature knob
controls.text: Turning this knob sets the temperature the heater should hold in automatic mode.
controls.context: The pilot sets it before pressing START.
